channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Lula sugere a Trump ‘tomar um trago’ com Xi e Putin; Renan Santos chama presidente de ‘bêbado safado’
item.description: At an event in Belo Horizonte, President Lula said he suggested Trump hold an informal chat with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin to ease global conflicts. The remark sparked reactions, including criticism from Renan Santos, who called Lula a 'drunk punk.' The episode revives debates over Brazil's foreign policy stance.

item.title: Lula falta ao debate da Band e defende investigação sobre o filho na Record
item.description: Lula skipped the Band debate and, in parallel, gave an interview to Record where he supported the PF investigation into his son. His absence changed the electoral coverage dynamics, shifting focus to candidates' parallel interviews.

item.title: Governo Lula tenta expandir contratação de MEIs por ministérios e estatais perto da eleição
item.description: President Lula's administration expands the hiring of individual micro-entrepreneurs by ministries and state-owned enterprises through the Contrata+ Brasil program, one week before the 2026 elections, aiming to boost his popularity among entrepreneurs.

item.title: Quaest: Moro lidera com folga e venceria qualquer um em 2º turno no Paraná
item.description: A Quaest poll released on August 24, 2026 shows Sergio Moro (PL) leading the race for Paraná governor with 37%, 16 points ahead of Requião Filho (PDT). In all second-round scenarios, Moro wins with comfortable margins, with a three-point margin of error and TSE registration under PR-05388/2026.

item.title: MP Eleitoral dá parecer favorável ao registro de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The Electoral Public Ministry issued a favorable opinion on Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential candidacy registration, stating he meets legal requirements and has no disqualifying convictions. The final decision rests with the Superior Electoral Court (TSE).

item.title: Mercosul segue sem acordo sobre divisão de cotas com a UE
item.description: Mercosul has not yet reached an agreement on the division of export quotas with the European Union, with Brazil and Paraguay holding opposing positions. Paraguay claims 25% of the quotas for each member country, while Brazil and Argentina advocate for criteria based on actual production and export volumes. The trade agreement has been provisionally in effect since May 1, 2026, but the internal distribution of quotas remains unresolved.

item.title: Carter Center se prepara para informar ao TSE que acompanhará a eleição brasileira
item.description: The Carter Center, the only U.S. organization invited by Brazil's TSE, confirmed it will observe the 2026 elections. The entity had withdrawn due to U.S. funding cuts but reversed its decision. In 2022, it certified the election's integrity and electronic voting reliability, while recommending stronger measures against disinformation.

item.title: Ancine aceita registro do filme “Dark Horse”
item.description: Ancine accepted the registration of the film "Dark Horse," about former president Jair Bolsonaro's trajectory. This is the first bureaucratic step for its theatrical release in Brazil, which still requires further stages.

item.title: Quaest no RS: Flávio Bolsonaro, 34%; Lula, 28%; Ronaldo Caiado, 3%; Renan Santos; 2%; Romeu Zema, 2%
item.description: Quaest poll in Rio Grande do Sul shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leading with 34% for the 2026 presidential race, followed by Lula (PT) at 28-29%. Lula's government approval stands at 38% with 55% disapproval. Other candidates like Ronaldo Caiado, Romeu Zema, Renan Santos and Pablo Marçal trail with single-digit support.

item.title: Quaest no RS: 45% desaprovam e 42% aprovam o governo Eduardo Leite
item.description: A Quaest poll in Rio Grande do Sul indicates that 45% of voters disapprove of Governor Eduardo Leite's administration, while 42% approve. Furthermore, 56% believe he does not deserve re-election.

item.title: Cármen Lúcia rejeita habeas corpus que tentava soltar Bolsonaro
item.description: STF Minister Cármen Lúcia rejected a habeas corpus petition seeking the release of former President Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year and 3-month sentence under house arrest. The decision cited procedural issues, including the lack of authorization from Bolsonaro himself and the absence of supporting evidence for the petitioner's claims.

item.title: Quaest: Moro lidera para governo do Paraná com 37%, Requião Filho tem 21% e sucessor de Ratinho Junior tem 15%
item.description: Quaest poll shows Sergio Moro (PL) leading Paraná gubernatorial race with 37%, followed by Requião Filho (PDT) at 21% and Sandro Alex (PSD), Ratinho Junior's successor, at 15%. In runoff simulations, Moro would defeat both rivals despite Ratinho Junior's high approval rating (79%).

item.title: Quaest no Paraná: Flávio Bolsonaro, 41%; Lula, 23%; Ronaldo Caiado, 5%; Romeu Zema, 3%; e Renan Santos, 2%
item.description: Quaest poll in Paraná shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leading with 41% for 2026 presidential race, followed by Lula (PT) at 23%. With Pablo Marçal included, Bolsonaro reaches 42%, Lula 24%, and Marçal 4%.

item.title: Haddad: Tarcísio diminuiu investimentos e queimou caixa; saímos de superávit para déficit
item.description: Fernando Haddad accused Tarcísio of reducing investments and causing a budget deficit in São Paulo. The PT candidate claims the current administration burned through reserves and shifted from surplus to deficit.

item.title: Pesquisas mostram a distância entre Lula e Flávio nos três maiores colégios eleitorais do país
item.description: Datafolha polls show Flávio Bolsonaro leading Lula in the second round in São Paulo (47% to 42%) and Rio de Janeiro (49% to 40%), while Lula has an edge in Minas Gerais (46% to 42%). Flávio's largest margin is 9 percentage points in Rio. In the first round, Flávio leads in all three states except Minas Gerais, where Lula tops with 37% against 31%.

item.title: Governo Lula lança teleatendimento a mulheres vítimas de violência
item.description: Lula's government launched a telehealth service for women facing violence, atypical mothers, and caregivers, offering psychological support with a keyword safety mechanism. Announced by Janja and the Health Minister, it is now nationwide via the Meu SUS Digital app, aiming for 100,000 monthly sessions.

item.title: Debate da Band: ataques a ausentes dominam um terço da repercussão digital, e cochilo de Kassab mobiliza a direita
item.description: The first Band debate was dominated by attacks on absent candidates Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, generating 53% of digital engagement, while proposals from present candidates received only 14%. Gilberto Kassab's nap mobilized the right wing, with 63% of comments coming from that political field, revealing internal disputes.

item.title: Moraes diz que Brasil tem ‘trauma’ com política de segurança pública e defende cooperação: ‘precisamos superar vaidades’
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes stated that Brazil has trauma regarding public security, linking this fear to past dictatorships, and advocated for cooperation between institutions to combat organized crime. He criticized the lack of information sharing among agencies, attributing it to vanities and the belief that 'information is power'. Moraes addressed these issues during a public hearing on the Anti-Facção Law.

item.title: Dr. Rosinha propõe regionalizar saúde e critica atual bancada paranaense no Senado
item.description: Dr. Rosinha (PT), candidate for the Senate in Paraná, proposed regionalizing healthcare to reduce risky patient transport on highways and criticized the detachment of current senators Sergio Moro and Oriovisto Guimarães. During the Tribuna do Norte interview, the former congressman also addressed infrastructure, public safety, agriculture, and international policy, aligning his proposals with President Lula's government.

item.title: Renan Santos e Romeu Zema defendem fim das bets e ex-governador de MG compara apostas com ‘cocaína’
item.description: Presidential candidates Renan Santos (Missão) and Romeu Zema (Novo) advocate for the abolition of online betting platforms in Brazil, proposing full prohibition and anti-addiction measures. Renan vows to 'destroy' betting sites and ties the issue to broader economic reforms, while Zema compares gambling addiction to cocaine use and labels the industry a 'plague'. Both emphasize protecting citizens from harmful practices.

item.title: Lula mira MEIs e flexibiliza compras públicas sem licitação
item.description: President Lula signed the Sicx decree, establishing a digital public procurement system without bidding processes, allowing government agencies to purchase directly from approved suppliers, including individual micro-entrepreneurs. The initiative aims to streamline contracting and boost local economies.

item.title: Randolfe prevê votação do fim da escala 6×1 na CCJ em 2 de setembro
item.description: Government leader in Congress, Senator Randolfe Rodrigues (PT-AP), announced that the Senate's CCJ is expected to vote on September 2 on the PEC ending the 6×1 work schedule. The proposal is one of the Lula administration's legislative priorities.

item.title: Renan Santos desembarca em BH nesta sexta e quer reunir apoiadores
item.description: Renan Santos arrives in Belo Horizonte to attend the first state congress of the Missão Party in Minas Gerais. The event on Friday (Aug 28) at TripFood Pampulha aims to mobilize supporters and organize the electoral campaign.

item.title: Saiba as datas dos próximos debates entre presidenciáveis
item.description: The first 2026 presidential debate, hosted by Band, gathered Renan Santos, Ronaldo Caiado, and Augusto Cury. Three more debates are scheduled before the first round on September 14th, 27th, and October 1st, broadcast by multiple media outlets. Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro did not attend the first debate, but the PT strategy considers Lula participating in only two forums.

item.title: Crusoé: Renan será o Ciro da direita?
item.description: Candidate Renan Santos shared an X post where a profile compares the right-wing's strategy with him to the left-wing's approach with Ciro Gomes. The discussion suggests Renan might be instrumentalized similarly to the former minister in a political maneuver.

item.title: Em reduto eleitoral de Ruas, Paes critica caça do PL a 'traidores': 'Vou lançar campanha anti bullying contra prefeitos'
item.description: Eduardo Paes criticized PL pressure on alliedmayors in São Gonçalo, announcing an 'anti-bullying' campaign against mayors and promising partnership with municipal managers. During a walk, he highlighted Douglas Ruas's father as an example of collaboration and attacked the opponent's management at the Cities Secretariat.

item.title: Ancine aceita registro de 'Dark Horse'
item.description: Ancine accepted the registration of 'Dark Horse', a film about Jair Bolsonaro awaiting release after the 2026 elections. The Federal Police are investigating alleged illicit funding by Daniel Vorcaro, while the cast is foreign and the release is scheduled for November.

item.title: Terras raras: empresa dos EUA avança na compra de mineradora no Brasil
item.description: U.S.-based USA Rare Earth secured $1.5 billion, including $750 million from the Department of Defense, to finalize the acquisition of Brazilian rare earth miner Serra Verde, operating at the Pela Ema mine in Goiás. The U.S. government also signed a contract to purchase at least $300 million in rare earth products, underscoring national security interests.

item.title: Flávio Dino autoriza Polícia Federal a acessar investigações sobre Dark Horse
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino authorized the Federal Police to access investigations into the funding of the film 'Dark Horse,' which portrays Jair Bolsonaro. The production is suspected of receiving irregular parliamentary amendments linked to producers associated with allies of the former president. Despite ongoing investigations, the film was cleared for theatrical release.

item.title: Torcidas organizadas se reúnem com elenco do São Paulo: "Salário atrasado"
item.description: São Paulo fan groups met with players and management to demand action after another loss to Chapecoense, deepening the club's crisis. Supporters cited delayed salaries and called for changes in leadership, as the team endures a 10-game winless run in the Brasileirão.

item.title: Campanha de Flávio aciona TSE contra Durigan e Lula
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign filed a complaint with the TSE against Finance Minister Dario Durigan and President Lula, alleging misuse of official agendas to promote Lula's reelection bid. The case was assigned to Justice André Mendonça.

item.title: Atual modelo eleitoral “faliu”, diz Moraes
item.description: Minister Alexandre de Moraes (STF) stated that Brazil's current electoral model "has failed" and advocated for urgent political reform during a speech at the National Congress of Public Law and External Control.

item.title: Tarcísio diz que disputa ao Planalto é 'projeto de Deus' após pastor citá-lo como presidente
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicans) addressed a potential 2030 presidential run after a pastor mentioned him as Brazil's future leader during an event. Tarcísio described the presidential bid as a 'God's project,' but stated that his current focus is winning reelection as São Paulo governor and that it is not yet time to discuss other elections.

item.title: Flávio aciona TSE contra ministro da Fazenda por suposto uso da máquina pública em campanha de Lula
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro filed a complaint with the TSE against Finance Minister Dario Durigan and Lula, alleging misuse of public resources for the PT campaign. The representation questions the overlap between Durigan's official duties and his role as economic spokesperson for Lula's candidacy.

item.title: PL à frente e PT em nono: ranking mostra os partidos com mais seguidores no Instagram entre os candidatos à Câmara
item.description: PL leads in Instagram followers among Chamber candidates with 110.5M, followed by PSD and MDB. PT ranks ninth overall but leads among left-wing parties. Distribution is unequal: 118 candidates hold 289M followers, while most have under 10K.

item.title: Globo entrevista Romeu Zema, candidato a presidente pelo Novo
item.description: Globo will conduct live interviews with the six top presidential candidates according to the Quaest poll from August 14, between August 24 and 29, right after Jornal Nacional. The first interview on August 24 will feature Romeu Zema (Novo), followed by Ronaldo Caiado, Renan Santos, Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, and Augusto Cury. The content will be broadcast on Globo, GloboNews, and g1, and will be available on Globoplay.

item.title: Por que Renan Santos liderou as atenções nas redes sociais durante o debate presidencial, segundo pesquisas
item.description: Renan Santos (Missão) led social media mentions during the first Band presidential debate with 38% favorable sentiment. Absentees Lula (53% negative) and Flávio Bolsonaro (49% negative) drew the most unfavorable mentions.

item.title: Flávio e Lula evitam ambientes não controlados para evitar questionamentos sobre Vorcaro e Lulinha
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro and Lula avoid uncontrolled environments to escape scrutiny over corruption and public safety failures, favoring televised debates where they maintain narrative control. Both rely on political alliances and seek to minimize exposure to direct criticism regarding security breakdowns and ongoing criminal investigations.

item.title: Ex-02 da PF refuta proposta de "Alcatraz" e defende colônias para presos trabalharem
item.description: Former federal penitentiary director Sandro Avelar criticizes 'jungle Alcatraz' proposals and advocates agricultural colonies for prisoner labor. He denounces supplier company lobbies blocking prison work programs and proposes reform requiring inmates to produce and reimburse state costs.

item.title: Artigo: as pesquisas não mudaram; a eleição, sim, ainda pode mudar
item.description: Recent polls show stable numbers despite major political scandals. The election could still change once the official campaign period begins, allowing candidates to build narratives and actively contest voter support beyond spontaneous exposure.

item.title: Deputado pede a Moraes investigação de aliado do clã Bolsonaro preso na Bolívia
item.description: Congressman Rui Falcão (PT-SP) requested Minister Alexandre de Moraes to expand investigations into Fernando Andrés Cerimedo, an ally of the Bolsonaro clan and Javier Milei, arrested in Bolivia. Cerimedo is suspected of running a 'bot farm' to spread disinformation against the Brazilian electoral system.

item.title: Tarcísio diz que candidatura ao Planalto é ‘projeto de Deus’ após pastor citá-lo como presidente
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas said a 2030 presidential run would be 'God's project' after a pastor referenced him as future president during a prayer. Still, he stressed his current focus is winning reelection and leaving a legacy in São Paulo. These remarks reinforce recent hints about his interest in running for the presidency.

item.title: Ministros do STF sinalizam que podem barrar trechos da Lei Antifacção e defendem diálogo com o Congresso
item.description: STF Justices Alexandre de Moraes and Gilmar Mendes signal they may strike down parts of the Anti-Faction Law, advocating dialogue with Congress and national coordination against organized crime. Moraes criticizes harsher penalties as ineffective and highlights judicial data management failures.

item.title: Ancine aprova registro de Dark Horse, filme sobre a vida de Jair Bolsonaro
item.description: Ancine approved the registration of the film 'Dark Horse' (O Azarão), which depicts the life of former president Jair Bolsonaro, allowing its exhibition in national theaters. Allies of Lula's campaign attempted to ban the screening during the electoral period at the TSE, but were unsuccessful. The film is under Federal Police investigation due to suspected irregular financing, including BRL 134 million requested by senator Flávio Bolsonaro from banker Daniel Vorcaro and funds from parliamentary amendments.

item.title: Crusoé: Renan vira alvo ao crescer fora da bolha
item.description: Renan Santos, candidate for president of the Missão party, was the most mentioned on social media after the Bandeirantes debate, with 88,000 mentions in 12 hours according to Datrix. Ronaldo Caiado came second with 35,000 mentions, and Augusto Cury also stood out. His growth outside the traditional media bubble has made Renan a new target of attacks.

item.title: Flávio acusa Durigan de fazer campanha para Lula enquanto ministro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) campaign filed a complaint with the TSE against Finance Minister Dario Durigan and President Lula, accusing Durigan of using institutional agendas to campaign for the PT candidate. The complaint, assigned to Minister André Mendonça, requests the preservation of ministerial records and documents, and seeks to prevent Durigan from participating in the GloboNews Debate, where he was presented as representing Lula's candidacy. The complaint is based on Durigan's participation in the 27th Santander Annual Conference, where he allegedly acted as a spokesperson for the president's government plan.

item.title: Lula sugere programa para ajudar clubes brasileiros endividados
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva revealed he suggested to Caixa Econômica Federal the creation of a program to renegotiate Brazilian football clubs' debts, similar to the Desenrola initiative. Lula attributed the clubs' indebtedness to poor management and the payment of astronomical salaries. However, the bank has not yet announced any concrete plan regarding the proposal.

item.title: Unicef: Renan Santos não aborda violência contra crianças no seu plano
item.description: UNICEF released an analysis of the government plans of the five presidential candidates with the highest voting intention and found that Renan Santos (Missão) does not explicitly address violence against children and adolescents, with only three mentions of the topic, all in the Education area. Among the other candidates, Ronaldo Caiado leads with 86 mentions, followed by Lula (37), Flávio Bolsonaro (28), and Romeu Zema (24), with proposals focused on criminal repression rather than prevention. The organization highlighted the absence of proposals addressing deaths resulting from police intervention in this age group and advocated combining prevention with repression.

item.title: Datafolha em Minas: PT vê Cleitinho no teto e chances no 2º turno
item.description: PT federal deputy Rogério Correia expressed optimism about Patrus Ananias reaching the second round of the Minas Gerais governor's race, assessing that Senator Cleitinho Azevedo (Republicanos) has already hit his electoral ceiling at 32% of voting intentions according to Datafolha. According to the PT member, Patrus has more room to grow than former mayor Alexandre Kalil (PDT), who is tied at 12%, especially with greater association with President Lula, who was in Belo Horizonte on the same day the poll was released.

item.title: Paulo Figueiredo defende ausência de Flávio em debates contra “irrelevantes”
item.description: Influencer Paulo Figueiredo defended Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) decision to skip presidential debates without Lula (PT) present. According to Figueiredo, Lula is Flávio's main opponent, making debates without the PT incumbent irrelevant. The strategy was shared in a post on X.
